extracted.intended_audience: Organizations participating in Google Maps Content Partners (PR/marketing teams preparing press releases or media communications)
extracted.subtask_short: press releases for Maps Content Partners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for organizations in the Google Maps Content Partners program to market and publicize their participation, specifically covering what to say, what not to disclose, approval procedures, and limits on media outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission to publicize participation
rubrics_metrics.description: You can market and publicize your organization's participation in Google Maps Content Partners. You can also promote our partnership in your organization's marketing communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure to use the guidelines below when you write a press release or talk to the media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be clear about our partnership
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell your organization that you've added to your organization's data to Google Maps and Google Earth. Explain how your organization and customers will benefit from how they can find and use your content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe concretely what was added to Google Maps/Earth and how users/customers will benefit or use that content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not overstate or disclose partnership terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not disclose the terms of your content license agreement unless you’re allowed to under our content license agreement's 'Publicity' and 'Confidentiality' provisions, if any. Do not say or imply that we have a relationship beyond your participation in Google Maps Content Partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sharing contractual/license details or implying broader relationships with Google than participation in the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not imply exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Your communications must clearly say you participate in Google Maps Content Partners. Do not say or imply that you have an exclusive agreement with Google.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use language that states participation (not exclusivity) and avoid phrasing that could be read as exclusive partnership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not share launch plans
rubrics_metrics.description: If we share launch plans with you, such as when your content will be published, do not share this information outside of your organization. Google doesn’t pre-announce new products or updates to products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat any Google-shared publication schedules or launch details as confidential; do not disclose them externally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press releases require Google review and approval
rubrics_metrics.description: All press releases that mention Google must be sent for review at least 7 business days before the announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To get approval, send a copy to press@google.com and include when you plan to issue the release, how you’ll distribute it, and who will get it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Google will not write joint press releases or join joint media outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Because we can’t accommodate all requests, we don't write joint releases. We also can’t participate in a joint media outreach. However, we can give a statement for your release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
You can ask for a custom Google statement or use the provided format; Google will give the name of the Google representative to attribute. Example suggested statement:

"We’re pleased to welcome [your organization's name] into Google's [program name] and to work with [description of your organization] to make their [type of map content] available to Google Maps and Google Earth users. By adding this content to Google's services, [your organization's name] will be able to [description of how users will benefit]."

rubrics_metrics.name: Wait for content publication before announcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not write a press release announcing your partnership with Google until your content is published on Google services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the organization's content is live on Google Maps/Earth before issuing any public announcement about the partnership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit frequency of press releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Only try to get one press release approved every 3 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit frequent/serial release requests; space requests to roughly one approved release per quarter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include personal Google contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include personal contact information for Google in your release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you’d like to include press contact information for Google, use press@google.com.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not speak for Google or its products
rubrics_metrics.description: You can conduct interviews and give statements about your organization's specific involvement. But do not speak for Google or speculate about any Google initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field press questions about Google, strategy, or products to Google (press@google.com). Only speak to your organization's specific role and involvement.
